A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with complete main text and Appendices A–C. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support comparison of the equations, figures, tables and supplementary material.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix C report original simulations and VECtor experiments, including accuracy, runtime, success rates and baseline comparisons.

after.justification: The same original simulation and real-world experimental results remain in Section 6 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The incidence and coplanarity solvers, translation recovery, Adam optimization and approximate-to-exact rotation cascade are unchanged in Sections 3–5 and Appendices A–B.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic line-event scenes and the same VECtor sequences: desk-normal, mountain-normal and sofa-normal. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 5 retains Gao et al.'s ICCV23 five-point solver and CVPR24 N-point solver as comparators. The solver variants compared in Tables 1 and 4 are also unchanged.

E3.justification: The evaluation metrics, 0.5-second simulation intervals, 0.3-second real-data intervals, downsampling to 5000 events and GC-RANSAC settings are identical.

E4.justification: Both retain the rotation-parametrization comparisons, event-count and line-count sensitivity tests, noise analyses, single-line failure analysis and objective landscapes in Section 6.1 and Appendix C.

E5.justification: The reported 1000-scene and 1000-trial simulation counts, median summaries, success rates and statistical displays are unchanged. No uncertainty-reporting procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: Results in Tables 1, 2, 4 and 5 and Figures 3–5 are identical. For example, Table 2 retains desk-normal IncBat errors of 0.232 for angular velocity and 23.0 degrees for linear-velocity direction.

T1.justification: The constant-velocity assumptions, incidence and coplanarity derivations, optimization formulations, and Appendix B pure-rotation propositions and proofs are identical. Figure 1 retains the same mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about full-DoF egomotion without additional sensors, novel coplanarity geometry, efficient optimization and pure-rotation handling.

C2.justification: The explanations of single-line ambiguity and optimization failures are unchanged. Appendix C.3 retains the same limitations concerning straight-line scenes, normal-flow quality and violations of constant velocity.

D1.justification: Implementation language, Adam defaults, initialization, hardware, preprocessing, robust-estimation parameters and the code-access statement are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the positioning relative to earlier geometric solvers, and all 58 references are unchanged.

P1.justification: The arXiv margin stamp changes from v1 dated 5 March 2025 to v2 dated 6 May 2025. Manuscript prose, terminology, headings and section order are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 changes from vector artwork to a raster rendering of the same diagram, with slightly different sizing and spacing. Its geometry, labels and caption are retained; all other figures and tables are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The revision updates the version stamp and the rendering of Figure 1, whose content and practical readability remain comparable. Methods, theory, experimental evidence, reproducibility information and appendices are unchanged, establishing no meaningful overall quality difference.
